sources.entry: Revel ⚠ - Community-focused event management and ticketing platform. (Demo, Source Code, Clients) MIT Python/Docker

summary.one_liner: Revel is an open-source, MIT-licensed event management, ticketing and membership platform for communities, clubs, venues and independent artists, with a hosted version and a self-hostable Docker stack.
summary.what_it_does: This repository is the Django/Django Ninja API behind Revel; the web app lives in revel-frontend and deployment in infra. Ticketing covers Stripe checkout, guest checkout, multiple tier types (fixed, pay-what-you-can, free, offline), discount codes, waitlists, refunds, QR tickets and Apple/Google Wallet passes. Memberships support recurring Stripe plans, series passes, and membership cards. Screening includes questionnaires, invitations, private guest lists, blacklists, and OpenID Connect login. The README also describes EU VAT handling (VIES checks, reverse charge, invoices), seat map designers, notifications via in-app, email and Telegram, Eventbrite sync, and XLSX/PDF exports. The README states that the platform's fee structure applies to the hosted service, and that self-hosting carries no fee to Revel.
use_cases: sell tickets for a club, gig or community event
manage recurring memberships for a studio or venue
issue wallet passes and check in attendees by QR scan
export attendee lists and VAT reports
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL> && cd infra && ./setup.sh (self-hosting wizard, in the infra repo)
Local development: make setup (first time only)
notable: No service fee added on top of ticket price for buyers; ticket money goes straight to the organizer's Stripe account
Questionnaire-based screening and invitation-only events built in as core features
Built-in seat maps in the free edition, with a box office view
EU VAT support including VIES validation and reverse charge
Apple Wallet and Google Wallet passes built in
caveats: Self-hosting needs a Linux x86-64 server with two DNS hostnames; the slim tier needs 2 vCPU and 4 GB RAM and the full tier 8 vCPU and 32 GB RAM
Without SMTP configured, nobody receives verification or ticket emails
Local development dev database runs on tmpfs and is empty after a container restart; needs native GDAL, GEOS, Pango, gettext and libmagic libraries
